meta.reinvestment_note: Interim cash is reinvested at 6.5% nominal and taxed at A11 on liquidation at the horizon.
meta.sale_costs_definition: Brokerage, title, escrow and legal (A09) plus county documentary transfer tax (S16), City of Los Angeles base transfer tax (S17) and Measure ULA where applicable (S17).

assumptions.name: Going-in cap rate for a central-LA single-tenant QSR
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: No official series publishes net-lease cap rates for this asset class (flagged F-05). The value is set by building up from the verified 10-year Treasury (4.84%, S02) plus a net-lease retail risk spread of roughly 90bp. A 90bp spread is at the tight end of what single-tenant quick-service trades have historically commanded, which is appropriate for a dense urban Southern California infill site with a national brand.
assumptions.materiality: HIGH — every downstream return is an inverse function of this number.
assumptions.how_to_replace: Substitute the broker's opinion of value or an actual appraisal; the model recomputes automatically.

assumptions.name: Long-run cap-rate risk spread over the 10-year Treasury
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Net-lease spreads have historically compressed in strong markets and widened sharply in stress. 90bp is a central estimate for an infill QSR in a supply-constrained metro.

assumptions.name: Rent growth while the existing lease runs
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: NNN leases commonly escalate at a flat 2% or at CPI with a collar. 2% is the modal contract structure. Note that this is BELOW observed LA CPI of 3.72% (S04), so in real terms the existing lease is designed to lose purchasing power — a point that favours the exit.

assumptions.name: Market rent growth at renewal
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Market rent at renewal should track the LA CPI observation (3.16% 2025 annual, S04) less a small structural drag for the county's declining population (S06, S09). Set at 2.75%, i.e. CPI minus roughly 40bp.

assumptions.name: Probability the tenant renews at SP-01
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Built from three verified signals, not intuition: (i) the tenant is closing 50–100 units in FY2026 by its own guidance (S12), which is an explicit negative; (ii) same-store sales improved from −7.1% to −1.1% (S13), which is an explicit positive; (iii) a unit-level urban LA location in a 4.8%-unemployment metro with a positive restaurant sub-sector (+7,300 jobs, S05) should sit in the stronger half of the portfolio. Net 62%, and the model reports 40% and 80% as bounds because this is the single most consequential unknown.

assumptions.name: Downtime if the tenant does NOT renew
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Months of vacancy plus rent abatement to re-tenant a 2,500–3,500 sq ft drive-through box in central LA.

assumptions.name: Re-tenanting cost if the tenant does not renew (TI plus leasing commission)
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Expressed as a percentage of property value, applied on rollover. Tenant improvements plus leasing commissions for a QSR box.

assumptions.name: Landlord retained capital reserve (roof, structure, parking, ADA)
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: A true triple-net lease pushes most costs to the tenant, but landlords routinely retain roof and structure. 35bp of value per year is a conservative reserve. If the lease is not genuinely NNN, this must rise (see flag F-01).

assumptions.name: Selling costs (brokerage, title, escrow, legal)
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Standard commercial transaction cost as a percentage of gross price. Excludes transfer tax, which is computed from S16 and S17.

assumptions.name: Owner's adjusted basis as a percentage of current value
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Unknown and unknowable without the owner's records (F-06). 40% represents a long-held asset. This drives the entire tax cost of selling, so the model reports the full range.
assumptions.privacy_note: Deliberately parameterised so that no actual basis figure is ever requested or stored.

assumptions.name: Blended tax rate on capital gain (federal + NIIT + California)
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: 20% federal long-term capital gains + 3.8% net investment income tax + 9.3% California ≈ 33.1%. Set at 33.4%. The top California bracket of 13.3% pushes the upper bound to 37.1%. Unrecaptured §1250 gain on depreciation is taxed at up to 25% and is NOT separately modelled — a known conservative simplification that if anything favours holding.

assumptions.name: Tenant's pricing power offset (mitigates rent-default risk)
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Applied as a haircut to the modelled probability of severe rent stress, reflecting that the franchisee can pass some cost inflation to menu price (S11 records 5.5% menu pricing in FY2025).

assumptions.name: Annualised probability of a regional black-swan event affecting the parcel
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Calibrated from verified history: two catastrophic urban wildfires hit Los Angeles County in the same week of January 2025, destroying 16,263 structures combined (S21 + S22). Over a 10-year hold a 2%/yr event probability implies a ~18% chance of at least one event. This is intentionally pessimistic relative to a calm-decade base rate, because the last decade produced two such events in one week.
assumptions.note: Deliberately NOT calibrated to a specific parcel, because the parcel is private (F-03).

assumptions.name: Severity of a black-swan event to the parcel (if it occurs)
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Loss of value as a fraction of gross value, after insurance recovery and before business interruption. A central-LA infill site is far less exposed than the wildland-urban interface that burned in 2025, so the base case is a partial impairment (shutdown, smoke and ash remediation, utility outage, six-to-eighteen months of zero rent) rather than total loss.

assumptions.name: Insurance recovery offset for a black-swan event
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: In a true NNN the tenant insures the building, so the landlord's direct property loss is partly covered. The landlord still absorbs rent interruption, deductible, and the post-event cap-rate widening that follows a regional catastrophe.

assumptions.name: Cap-rate penalty for short remaining lease term
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Buyers of single-tenant assets price renewal risk. Below roughly five years of remaining term, quoted cap rates widen materially and the asset becomes a re-leasing story rather than a bond. Modelled as +75bp at zero remaining term, scaled linearly.
assumptions.note: This single assumption is why 'sell before expiry' can beat 'hold to expiry' even when rents are rising.

assumptions.name: Secular demand drag from county population decline
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: The verified fact is that LA County lost 3.2% of its population in five years (S06) and is projected to lose a further 240,800 K-12 students in ten (S09). The modelled mechanism is a 25bp annual drag on real rent growth. This is a disclosed judgement, not an observation.

assumptions.name: Property value scenario bands used for reporting
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: The property's actual value is private. Three bands are run because they straddle the two Measure ULA thresholds ($5.4M and $10.9M), so the tax cliff is visible rather than averaged away. The $6.5M band is the reporting base case. The ranking of strategies is stable across all three bands.
assumptions.materiality: N/A (reporting parameter, not a market input)

assumptions.name: Reinvestment rate on interim after-tax cash
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Interim cash must be put somewhere or the comparison between a 2026 exit and a 2052 exit is meaningless. 6.5% is set above the verified 10-year Treasury of 4.84% (S02) to reflect a diversified income portfolio with some equity risk, and below a fair-return assumption for direct real estate. Reinvestment growth is taxed at A11 on liquidation.

assumptions.name: Blended tax rate applied to growth of the reinvestment portfolio
assumptions.label: ASSUMPTION
assumptions.basis: Lower than A11 because a diversified portfolio turns over partially, realising some long-term gains at preferential rates and deferring the rest. Used only for the reinvestment sleeve, never for the property itself.
